evals.name: implement
evals.prompt: Choose a segmented control for an exclusive filter. Give the component boundary and a check for the resulting interaction.
evals.expected_output: For a small exclusive choice use ToggleGroup with one string value. Distinguish a filter choice from revealing a panel; they promise different keyboard behavior.
assertions: Name the value and commit boundary. Done: the scope has one key and Apply is the only action that changes the active filter.
Give the group an accessible name and keep draft selection controlled. Done: one tab stop reaches the group and arrow navigation moves to the other option.

evals.name: diagnose
evals.prompt: My scope control takes four tab stops. Give the component boundary and a check for the resulting interaction.
evals.expected_output: If changing a choice should reveal a different labeled panel, use tabs instead of assigning tab roles to a value picker.
assertions: If changing a choice should reveal a different labeled panel, use tabs instead of assigning tab roles to a value picker.
Give the group an accessible name and keep draft selection controlled. Done: one tab stop reaches the group and arrow navigation moves to the other option.
Follow selection with Tab and activate Apply. Done: Mine receives keyboard focus while the active value is still all; Apply commits mine.
